judge.summary: The agent read the current code and history, decided that the LR and batch-size axes were near saturation, and chose the missing clean architecture probe: increasing DEPTH from 8 to 9 while holding MODEL_DIM fixed at 512. It replaced the ASPECT_RATIO-derived width calculation with a fixed MODEL_DIM constant, set DEPTH = 9, committed, and ran one experiment. The run completed successfully with val_bpb = 1.017268, peak VRAM 25.3 GB, 57.7M params, and 226.5M tokens. This improved the current best of 1.017604 by only 0.000336, below the required 0.0005 margin, so it was not a valid improvement.
judge.feedback: The implementation was correct and the run did not crash; the failure was in experiment selection. The decisive mistake was choosing a change whose expected or realized gain was likely below the acceptance threshold: pure depth 8 -> 9 at fixed width 512 added ~15% parameters and ~10% fewer training tokens, yielding only a 0.000336 gain. Because the task requires beating the best by more than 0.0005, a marginal architecture probe is not sufficient unless it can be made stronger or more compute-efficient. The agent should have either chosen a higher-leverage untried change or coupled the depth increase with a compensating efficiency change large enough to plausibly produce a bigger net gain, rather than accepting an apparent sub-threshold improvement.
